workflowInfo.workflowDescription: Audits RACF keyring certificate expiry dates and POSTs an alert to a CSP REST endpoint when certificates are expiring or already expired. Uses user/password or OAuth 2.0 bearer token authentication.

variable.name: KEYRING_OWNER
variable.label: Keyring Owner User ID
variable.abstract: The RACF user ID that owns the keyring to audit
variable.description: The RACF user ID associated with the keyring. For the default z/OSMF keyring this is IZUSVR. For a Zowe keyring the default is ZWESIUSR.

variable.name: KEYRING_NAME
variable.label: Keyring Name
variable.abstract: The name of the RACF keyring to audit
variable.description: The keyring label associated with KEYRING_OWNER. Example: IZUKeyring.IZUDFLT

variable.name: WARN_DAYS
variable.label: Warning Threshold (days)
variable.abstract: Flag any certificate expiring within this many days
variable.description: Certificates expiring within this many days are reported as WARNING. Certificates already past their expiry date are always reported as EXPIRED. Set to 0 to report expiry dates only without a warning threshold.

variable.name: REXX_DATASET
variable.label: REXX EXEC Library
variable.abstract: PDS containing the KEYRGAUD member used by the expiry audit step
variable.description: The partitioned dataset (PDS or PDSE) that contains the KEYRGAUD REXX exec. The exec is called by the auditExpiry step via IKJEFT01. Example: ANDRE.REXX.EXEC

variable.name: STAGE_DATASET
variable.label: Staging Dataset
variable.abstract: Pre-allocated sequential dataset used to stage the audit report between steps
variable.description: A pre-allocated sequential dataset (LRECL=132, RECFM=FB or VB) used to hold the audit report so the notifyCSP step can read it and build the alert payload. Must exist and be catalogued before the workflow runs. Example: ANDRE.CERT.REPORT

variable.name: CSP_ENDPOINT
variable.label: CSP REST Endpoint URL
variable.abstract: Full URL of the CSP REST API endpoint that accepts alert events
variable.description: The complete HTTPS URL of the CSP event ingest endpoint. Example: https://csp.example.com/api/v1/events Only HTTPS is recommended for production use.

variable.name: CSP_AUTH_TYPE
variable.label: CSP Authentication Type
variable.abstract: Authentication scheme used when calling the CSP REST API (BASIC or BEARER)
variable.description: Set to BASIC to use HTTP Basic Authentication (user/password). Set to BEARER to supply an OAuth 2.0 bearer token via CSP_TOKEN. The chosen scheme controls which Authorization header is built by the notifyCSP step.

variable.name: CSP_USER
variable.label: CSP User ID (Basic Auth)
variable.abstract: CSP user ID used when CSP_AUTH_TYPE is BASIC
variable.description: The CSP service account user ID used for HTTP Basic Authentication. Ignored when CSP_AUTH_TYPE is BEARER.

variable.name: CSP_PASSWORD
variable.label: CSP Password (Basic Auth)
variable.abstract: CSP password used when CSP_AUTH_TYPE is BASIC
variable.description: The CSP service account password. Stored as a private variable so it is masked in the z/OSMF UI. Ignored when CSP_AUTH_TYPE is BEARER.

variable.name: CSP_TOKEN
variable.label: CSP OAuth 2.0 Bearer Token
variable.abstract: Bearer token used when CSP_AUTH_TYPE is BEARER
variable.description: The OAuth 2.0 access token for CSP API calls. Stored as a private variable so it is masked in the z/OSMF UI. Ignored when CSP_AUTH_TYPE is BASIC.

variable.name: SYSTEM_NAME
variable.label: System Name
variable.abstract: z/OS system name to include in the alert payload (e.g. SY1)
variable.description: The MVS system name or SMFID of this z/OS image. Included in the CSP alert payload so the receiving team can identify which system raised the alert. Example: SY1 or PROD1

variable.name: AUDIT_VERDICT
variable.label: Audit Verdict
variable.abstract: CLEAN, WARNING, or EXPIRED – set by the evaluateAudit step
variable.description: The overall verdict of the certificate expiry audit. CLEAN means no certificates are expiring or expired. WARNING means at least one certificate will expire within WARN_DAYS days. EXPIRED means at least one certificate has already passed its expiry date.

variable.name: ALERT_PAYLOAD
variable.label: CSP Alert JSON Payload
variable.abstract: JSON body to be POSTed to the CSP event endpoint
variable.description: The JSON payload assembled by the evaluateAudit step and consumed by the notifyCSP rest step. Contains the alert severity, system name, keyring details, and the first expiring certificate found.

step.name: auditExpiry
step.title: Audit Certificate Expiry Dates
step.description: Runs the KEYRGAUD REXX exec via IKJEFT01 to enumerate every certificate in the target keyring and flag those expiring within WARN_DAYS days. Output is routed to STAGE_DATASET for use by subsequent steps.
step.instructions:
Audits every certificate connected to keyring ${instance-KEYRING_NAME} owned by ${instance-KEYRING_OWNER}, flagging certificates that expire within ${instance-WARN_DAYS} days.
The report is written to ${instance-STAGE_DATASET} for downstream processing. The dataset must already exist and be catalogued.
Pre-requisites: - KEYRGAUD must be installed in ${instance-REXX_DATASET}(KEYRGAUD). - ${instance-STAGE_DATASET} must be pre-allocated (LRECL>=132).

step.name: evaluateAudit
step.title: Evaluate Audit and Build Alert Payload
step.description: Reads the staged audit report, determines the overall verdict (CLEAN / WARNING / EXPIRED), and assembles the JSON payload that will be POSTed to CSP. Sets AUDIT_VERDICT and ALERT_PAYLOAD.
step.instructions:
Reads ${instance-STAGE_DATASET}, scans for EXPIRED and WARNING lines, derives AUDIT_VERDICT, and writes the JSON alert payload to /tmp/csp_payload_${instance-SYSTEM_NAME}.json for the notifyCSP step.
If AUDIT_VERDICT is CLEAN the notifyCSP and logResult steps still run but the CSP call records severity INFO rather than WARNING or CRITICAL.

template.inlineTemplate:
#!/bin/sh # ------------------------------------------------------------------- # evaluateAudit – parse the KEYRGAUD report and build the CSP payload # ------------------------------------------------------------------- REPORT_DS="${instance-STAGE_DATASET}" SYSTEM="${instance-SYSTEM_NAME}" OWNER="${instance-KEYRING_OWNER}" RING="${instance-KEYRING_NAME}" WARN_DAYS="${instance-WARN_DAYS}" PAYLOAD_FILE="/tmp/csp_payload_${SYSTEM}.json"
# Read the staged report from the MVS dataset via //'DSN' REPORT=$(cat "//'${REPORT_DS}'" 2>/dev/null) if [ $? -ne 0 ]; then echo "ERROR: cannot read staging dataset //'${REPORT_DS}'" exit 1 fi
# Count EXPIRED and WARNING lines EXPIRED_COUNT=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -c "EXPIRED" || true) WARN_COUNT=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -c "WARNING" || true)
# Derive overall verdict if [ "$EXPIRED_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then VERDICT="EXPIRED" SEVERITY="critical" elif [ "$WARN_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then VERDICT="WARNING" SEVERITY="warning" else VERDICT="CLEAN" SEVERITY="info" fi
echo "AUDIT_VERDICT=${VERDICT} (EXPIRED=${EXPIRED_COUNT} WARNING=${WARN_COUNT})"
# Extract first flagged certificate label for the payload summary FIRST_CERT=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 -E "EXPIRED|WARNING" | sed 's/ */ /g' | cut -c1-120 || true) if [ -z "$FIRST_CERT" ]; then FIRST_CERT="No expiring certificates detected." fi
# Escape double-quotes in FIRST_CERT for JSON safety FIRST_CERT_ESCAPED=$(echo "$FIRST_CERT" | sed 's/"/\\"/g')
# Build timestamp (USS date in ISO-8601 form) TIMESTAMP=$(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ" 2>/dev/null || date +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")
# Write JSON payload cat > "${PAYLOAD_FILE}" << ENDJSON { "source": "z/OS-${SYSTEM}", "event_type": "certificate_expiry_audit", "severity": "${SEVERITY}", "timestamp": "${TIMESTAMP}", "keyring_owner": "${OWNER}", "keyring_name": "${RING}", "warn_threshold_days": ${WARN_DAYS}, "expired_count": ${EXPIRED_COUNT}, "warning_count": ${WARN_COUNT}, "verdict": "${VERDICT}", "first_flagged_cert": "${FIRST_CERT_ESCAPED}" } ENDJSON
echo "Payload written to ${PAYLOAD_FILE}" cat "${PAYLOAD_FILE}"
# Surface verdict as a parseable token for setVariable echo "__VERDICT__${VERDICT}__"

step.name: notifyCSP
step.title: POST Alert to CSP
step.description: Sends the JSON alert payload assembled by evaluateAudit to the CSP REST endpoint using curl. Supports HTTP Basic Authentication (CSP_AUTH_TYPE=BASIC) or OAuth 2.0 Bearer token (CSP_AUTH_TYPE=BEARER). The step fails if CSP returns a non-2xx HTTP status code.
step.instructions:
POSTs the alert JSON to ${instance-CSP_ENDPOINT} using ${instance-CSP_AUTH_TYPE} authentication.
- BASIC: supply CSP_USER and CSP_PASSWORD. - BEARER: supply CSP_TOKEN (OAuth 2.0 access token).
A CSP response code outside 200–299 causes this step to fail. The HTTP response body is printed to SYSOUT for diagnostics.
Note: curl must be available in the USS PATH on this system. On z/OS 2.4+ curl ships with z/OS Open Tools or IBM Ported Tools.

template.inlineTemplate:
#!/bin/sh # ------------------------------------------------------------------- # notifyCSP – POST the alert payload to the CSP REST endpoint # ------------------------------------------------------------------- ENDPOINT="${instance-CSP_ENDPOINT}" AUTH_TYPE="${instance-CSP_AUTH_TYPE}" CSP_USER="${instance-CSP_USER}" CSP_PASSWORD="${instance-CSP_PASSWORD}" CSP_TOKEN="${instance-CSP_TOKEN}" SYSTEM="${instance-SYSTEM_NAME}" PAYLOAD_FILE="/tmp/csp_payload_${SYSTEM}.json"
if [ ! -f "${PAYLOAD_FILE}" ]; then echo "ERROR: payload file ${PAYLOAD_FILE} not found – did evaluateAudit complete?" exit 1 fi
echo "Sending alert to CSP endpoint: ${ENDPOINT}" echo "Auth type: ${AUTH_TYPE}" echo "Payload:" cat "${PAYLOAD_FILE}" echo ""
# Build the curl auth flag based on authentication type if [ "${AUTH_TYPE}" = "BEARER" ]; then AUTH_FLAG="-H \"Authorization: Bearer ${CSP_TOKEN}\"" else # Default: BASIC AUTH_FLAG="-u \"${CSP_USER}:${CSP_PASSWORD}\"" fi
# POST to CSP – capture HTTP status code HTTP_STATUS=$(eval curl -s -o /tmp/csp_response_${SYSTEM}.txt -w "%{http_code}" \ -X POST "${ENDPOINT}" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ ${AUTH_FLAG} \ --data-binary "@${PAYLOAD_FILE}" \ --max-time 30 \ --retry 2 \ --retry-delay 5 \ --insecure 2>&1)
CURL_RC=$? echo "curl exit code : ${CURL_RC}" echo "CSP HTTP status : ${HTTP_STATUS}" echo "CSP response body:" cat /tmp/csp_response_${SYSTEM}.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "(empty)" echo ""
if [ ${CURL_RC} -ne 0 ]; then echo "ERROR: curl failed with exit code ${CURL_RC}" exit 1 fi
# Accept any 2xx status code as success STATUS_CLASS=$(echo "${HTTP_STATUS}" | cut -c1-1) if [ "${STATUS_CLASS}" != "2" ]; then echo "ERROR: CSP returned HTTP ${HTTP_STATUS} – expected 2xx" exit 1 fi
echo "SUCCESS: Alert delivered to CSP (HTTP ${HTTP_STATUS})"

step.name: logResult
step.title: Log Notification Result
step.description: Prints a final summary to SYSOUT confirming the audit verdict and the CSP notification outcome. This step always runs regardless of verdict so there is always a visible audit trail in JES.

template.inlineTemplate: #!/bin/sh echo "========================================================" echo " Certificate Expiry CSP Notification – Result Summary" echo "========================================================" echo " System : ${instance-SYSTEM_NAME}" echo " Keyring owner : ${instance-KEYRING_OWNER}" echo " Keyring name : ${instance-KEYRING_NAME}" echo " Verdict : ${instance-AUDIT_VERDICT}" echo " CSP endpoint : ${instance-CSP_ENDPOINT}" echo " Timestamp : $(date -u +'%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ')" echo "========================================================" echo " Workflow complete."
